Cases of nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain and fever were reported from Village Kathwada, Sub-District Daskroi, District Ahmadabad. District RRT investigated the outbreak. All cases were residents of Gujarat Housing Board Society, Kathwada, Nikol Ward, East Zone. The affected age group was 2-40 years. Cases were treated at a medical camp established in the locality. 10 patients were treated at DH Singarwa. 1 serum sample collected, tested positive for S. typhi by widal test. 8 water samples collected, tested positive for residual chlorine in OT test. Water pipeline leakages were repaired. Chlorination of water sources was done. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water and food habits, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of loose motion and vomiting were reported from Village Shankrpur, UPHC Zundal, District Gandhinagar. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was done. Medicine and ORS packets were given to cases. Chlorination of water sources was done. 3 .water samples collected and sent to GMERS Vadnagar were potable. Both children and adults

Cases of loose motion, vomiting and abdominal pain were reported from Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya (KGBV), Model Residential School, Sub-District Satlasana, District Mahesana. District RRT investigated the outbreak. All cases were treated at GMERS Vadnagar. The affected age group was 13-18 years. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe food habits, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of loose motion, vomiting and abdominal pain were reported from Kanade area, UHC Pardi, District Surat. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases fell ill after consuming snacks in a shop opening ceremony. All cases were treated at health facilities and recovered. The affected age group was 3-68 years. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on vector control measures, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of fever with chills were reported from Village Churgi, Sub- District Chaibasa, District West Singhbhum. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house fever survey was done. Cases were treated at CHC Manoharpur. The affected age group was 1-60 years. Out of 69 blood samples collected, 32 samples tested positive

Cases of loose stools, vomiting, abdominal pain and fever were reported among students residing at the Government Girls Hostel, Village Ijarilakmapura under Devagiri UPHC Haveri, Taluk Haveri, District Haveri. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected age group was 15-44 years. All cases were admitted to Veerapura Multispeciality Hospital. 4 stool samples, 2 blood samples, and 1 drinking water sample were tested at DPHL, Haveri. 1 water sample was analysed using MPN and subculture showed growth of Escherichia coli, indicating that the water source was unfit for human consumption. 4 stool samples were negative for hanging drop, ova and cyst. Culture yielded no enteric pathogen. 2 Blood cultures were incubated and subcultured periodically; culture were sterile after 7 days of aerobic incubation. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water and food habits, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of fever, jaundice, nausea, and vomiting and general weakness were reported from Mar Athanasius College, Sub-District Kothamangalam, District Ernakulam. District RRT investigated the outbreak. All cases were treated at health facilities. The affected age group was 13-55 years. Out of 12 water samples collected and sent to RPH Lab Ernakulam, 1 sample showed presence of Coliform bacteria. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, food habits, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of loose stools, vomiting, abdominal pain and mild fever were reported from Village Puthenvelikkara (CT), Sub-District Paravur, District Ernakulam. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Patients of all age groups were affected. The cases had consumed food items from a temporary food stall. 3 water samples were collected from the water sources and sent to RPH Lab, Ernakulam. Coliforms were detected in 2 samples. 2 stool samples were tested at the Microbiology Department of Govt. Medical College and were negative on bacteriological analysis. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral

Cases of fever, myalgia, abdominal pain, vomiting and jaundice were reported from Olive Wood stocks Apartment, Palarivattom, Sub-district Kochi, District Ernakulam. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected age group was 17-59 years. All cases were treated symptomatically and patients were isolated. 2 water samples collected and tested at RPHL EKM, showed presence of coliforms. 2 serum samples collected, tested positive for Hepatitis A (IgM ELISA). Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water and food habits, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of diarrhea, vomiting, nausea and abdominal pain were reported from Village Koduvayur-II, Sub- District Chittur, District Palakkad. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected age group was 4-75 years. Cases had attended a housewarming ceremony. One rectal swab was tested for culture at the Integrated Public Health Laboratory, Palakkad and was found to be negative for Salmonella and Shigella. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking

Cases of fever with rash were reported from Villages Chhota Hingoria (16 cases), Takrawad (10 cases) and sarwaniya (2 cases), Sub- District Malhargarh, District Mandsaur. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Active search for fever cases was done. 28 epidemiologically linked cases in the three villages were given symptomatic treatment. The affected age group was below 15 years of age. All 4 blood samples collected, tested positive for Measles (IgM ELISA). Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on isolation of cases, hygiene maintenance and proper nutrition.

Cases of fever with altered sensorium were reported from Mehboobpura, Sub-District Nagpur (Urban), District Nagpur. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house fever survey was done. The affected age group was 23-61 years. 10 serum samples were collected for JE and tested at IGGMC, Nagpur and all samples were negative (IgM ELISA). Entomological investigation was conducted (CI-8, HI- 7.5, BI- 6.5). Anti-larval activities and fogging was done in the affected area. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on vector

Cases of loose motion and abdominal pain were reported from Village Bagabasa, Sub-District Khunta, District Mayurbhanj. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The most affected age group was 44-59 years. The cases had consumed food in a funeral ceremony. All cases were treated. 2 water samples were tested at DPHL Mayurbhanj for H S and OT 2 test. The OT level was <0.01 ppm, and H₂S test results were negative. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water and food habits, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of diarrhoea, vomiting and giddiness were reported from Village Vadachennimalai, Block Thalaivasal, District Salem. District RRT investigated the outbreak. 7 water samples, 7 stool samples were collected and tested at DPHL Mettur, and GMKMCH Salem. Stool samples were examined by hanging drop preparation and culture, water samples were tested for coliforms, Coliform bacteria were detected in all 7 water samples, while the remaining samples tested negative. Chlorination of water sources was done. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water and food habits, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of loose motion and abdominal discomfort were reported from Village Dharmatala, Sub-District Purbasthali - I, District Purba Bardhaman. District RRT investigated the outbreak. People fell ill after eating food at a community gathering. Cases were treated at RH Srirampur. 2 stool samples were tested for culture and were found to be negative. Cases of all age groups were affected. All cases recovered. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water and food habits, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases with symptoms of fever with parotid gland swelling were reported from Blossom International Residential School, Panipara, Sub-District Kothamangalam, District Ernakulam. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The cases were 4-year old students. All cases were treated symptomatically. Cases were clinically diagnosed with Mumps. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on the spread of disease, isolation of cases, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of abdominal pain with vomiting were reported from Village Manlaw, Block Haswa, Sub-District Fatehpur, District Fatehpur. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected age group was 20-65 years. Cases had consumed finger chips from a fast-food cart. Soon after consuming the food, their health deteriorated, following which they were admitted to Thariyaon CHC for treatment. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water and food habits, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of fever and body ache were reported from Village Ramdevpur (17 cases), & Satmesara (15 cases), Sub-District Kerakat, District Jaunpur. District and Block RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house fever survey was done. The affected age group was 19-56 years. All 32 Blood samples collected, tested negative for Dengue and malaria (RDT). 7 blood samples tested positive for Orientia tsutsugamushi (IgM ELISA) at IMS BHU. 1 death was reported in a 40-years old- female who was positive for scrub typhus. Anti-larval activities were done in the affected area. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on vector control measures, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of fever with body pain were reported from Village Abhay Chand Patti, Sub- District/District Jaunpur. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house fever survey was done. Cases were treated at CHC Karnjakala. Out of 12 blood samples collected and sent to IMS BHU, 3 samples tested positive for O. tsutsugamushi (IgM ELISA). Source reduction activities were done in the affected area. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on vector control measures, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Villages Phulguri Nepali, Barpukhuri Par, Sirajuli Pathar, Oriontoli, Singitali, Mazgaon, Dauka Chuburi, Hirajuli TE, Bhalukjaroni, Kathaldup, Chilabandha, Naharbari, Jamidarichuk, Sub-districts Chariduar, Dhekiajuli (Pt) and Tezpur of District Sonitpur. Cases presented with symptoms of acute fever, headache, unconsciousness and change in mental status. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases were in the age group 6 - 68 years. 100 CSF and serum samples of AES cases were collected and sent to SRL-TMCH and DPHL-KCH Sonitpur. Out of these samples, 13 tested positive for Japanese Encephalitis (IgM ELISA). 4 deaths were reported: 51-year-old female on 25.06.2025, 36-year-old male on 8.07.2025, 10-year-old male on 12.07.2025, and a 6-year-old female on 13.07.2025. The cause of 4 deaths was confirmed to be Japanese Encephalitis. IEC activities and vector control measures were conducted. Fever surveillance was conducted and fogging operations were carried out. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on vector control measures, health seeking behaviour, vaccination, hygiene and sanitation

Cases were reported from Village Markapal, Sub-District Bhairamgarh, District Bijapur. The cases presented with symptoms of fever with chills. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house fever survey was done in the affected area. Cases were in the age group 5-49 years. Cases were treated with antimalarial medication. Out of 160 blood samples collected during malaria mukt abhiyan and tested at CHC Bhairamgarh using RDT, 9 samples were positive for malaria (7 Plasmodium falciparum and 2 Plasmodium vivax). Vector control measures were undertaken. Community awareness was given. Source Reduction activities were conducted.

Cases were reported from Village Hardi, Sub-District Akaltara, District Janjgir Champa. Cases presented with symptoms of loose motion and vomiting. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Majority of the cases were in the age group 15-60 years. Cases were treated symptomatically at a health camp organized in the locality. 1 Stool sample was collected and sent to District Hospital Janjgir tested negative for cholera by culture. Public health measures were taken, such as water chlorination by the PHE department, distribution of chlorine tablets and bleaching powder, and health education on hand hygiene, consumption of boiled water. Community awareness was done by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene maintenance and proper sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Changa, Sub-District Petlad, Anand. The cases presented with loss of appetite, anorexia and abdominal pain. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases were in the age group 5-44 years. Cases were treated at CHC Petlad. Out of 11 blood samples tested at SSG Hospital Vadodara, 8 samples were positive for Hepatitis A (IgM ELISA). Out of 22 water samples collected and sent to S.S Hospital Petlad, 7 samples were unsatisfactory for drinking purpose. Pipeline leakages were repaired by PHED. Chlorination of water sources was done in the locality. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Kanagar, Sub-District Danta, District Banas Kantha. Cases presented with symptoms of loose watery stools and vomiting. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases were in the age group 5-60 years. Cases were treated at CHC Danta. 2 stool samples were collected and sent to Banas General Hospital Palanpur tested negative for cholera by culture. A 3-year- old male expired on 27.07.2025 with acute gastroenteritis, severe dehydration, shock and AKD. Chlorine tablets were distributed to households. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Narigram area, UPHC Akhlol Jakatnaka, District Bhavnagar. Cases presented with symptoms of diarrhea, vomiting and severe dehydration.District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases were in the age group 5-44 years. Cases were treated at a health camp organized in the locality. 1 stool sample collected and sent to Sir T Hospital tested negative for V. cholerae (culture). Out of 3 water samples sent to Government Medical College Bhavnagar, 2 samples were non-potable. Chlorine tablets distributed to households. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from the Urban area of UPHC/Sub-District Sidhpur, District Patan. Cases presented with symptoms of nausea and abdominal pain. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases were in the age group 5-25 years. Cases were treated at UPHC Sidhpur. 2 water samples collected and sent to General Hospital Sidhpur were unsatisfactory for drinking purpose. All 16 blood samples collected and sent to SDH Sidhpur tested positive for Hepatitis A (IgM ELISA). Chlorination of water sources was done in the locality. Pipeline leakages were repaired by PHED. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Chaharon, Sub Center-Munda khera, CHC Chhachhrauli, District Yamuna Nagar. The cases presented with symptoms of stomach pain, loose watery stools and headache. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases were treated at a health camp organized in the locality and at CHC Chhachhrauli. All age groups ≥ 5 years were affected. 7 stool samples were collected and sent to DPHL (IDSP) Yamuna Nagar tested negative for cholera by culture. All 11 blood samples collected tested negative for Hepatitis A & E (IgM ELISA). 4 water samples were collected and sent to DPHL (IDSP) for bacteriological test were found unfit for drinking purpose. ORS packets were distributed. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of fever with rash were reported from Village Pipradih, CHC Bermo, Sub- district Chandrapura, District Bokaro. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Active search for fever cases done in the locality. Cases were in the age group 4 - 48 years. All cases were treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on isolation of cases, hygiene maintenance and proper nutrition.

Cases of loose motion and vomiting were reported from Village Amainagar, Sub- District Ghatshila. District East Singhbhum. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases were treated at a health camp organized in the village. Cases were in the age group 2 - 65 years. ORS packets were distributed to cases. 3 water samples were collected and sent to MGM VRDL lab Jamshedpur showed presence of Enterococcus faecalis. Chlorine tablets were distributed to households. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene and sanitation

Cases were reported from Village Shankavarampalli, PHC Mittemari, Sub- district Bagepalli, District Chikkaballapura. Cases presented with symptoms of vomiting and loose motion. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases were in the age group 8 -78 years. Nearly 400 people attended a death ceremony. The lunch served was contaminated with rainfall and the food preparation area was unhygienic. Cases were treated symptomatically. 1 stool sample was collected and sent to DPHL Chikballapur showed growth of no pathogens. 2 water samples tested with H₂S media were found potable. Community awareness and health education was given by peripheral team on safe food habits, hygiene and sanitation. House-to-house survey was done by health staff and ASHA workers to identify any new cases.

Cases were reported from Bharathi Excellence School, Village Mellahalli, CHC K.M. Doddi, Sub-district Maddur, District Mandya. Cases presented with symptoms of loose motion and vomiting. Cases were in the age group 3 - 42 years. District and Block RRT visited the school and conducted an inspection of the hostel and water supply. Food prepared at the hostel was suspected to be contaminated. Cases were treated at a health camp organized in the school premises. Out of 3 water samples collected and sent to DPHL Mandya, 2 samples were non-potable. 3 stool samples were collected and tested at MIMS, Mandya (Hanging drop test) and 2 stool samples were collected and tested at MMC, Mysore (culture and sensitivity) showed growth of no pathogens. IEC activities were conducted. The Education Department was informed of preventive action in the school hostel. The school authorities, hostel warden, and headmaster were instructed to supply purified drinking water and ensure regular cleaning of the water tanks.

Cases were reported from Village Byalyal, PHC Huvina Hipparagi, Sub-district Basavana Bagewadi, District Vijayapura. Cases presented with symptoms of loose stool and vomiting. The most affected age group was 5-10 years. District RRT investigated the outbreak. There was a contaminated borewell near a stream, which was submerged due to rainfall and surrounded by open-air defecation sites considered as the possible source of water contamination. A temporary OPD clinic was established at the Anganwadi center for treatment of cases. Out of 7 water samples collected and tested at DPHL Vijayapur, 3 samples were found unfit for human consumption. All 3 stool samples collected and tested at DPHL Vijayapur were negative for cholera with only normal commensals isolated. Alternate water supply was arranged in the village. Cleaning and chlorination of OHTs and pipelines and bacteriological testing before water supply was done. Drilling of a new borewell was done to ensure safe water. Community awareness and health education was given regarding safe drinking water, hygiene maintenance and proper nutrition.

Cases were reported from N-Able Training Institution, Karimakkad Ward-38, UPHC Thrikakara, District Ernakulam. The cases presented with symptoms of loose stools and vomiting. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected age group was 17 - 38 years. Cases were treated symptomatically. 2 stool samples were collected and sent to NIV Alappuzha, which tested PCR negative for the viral panel. 2 water samples tested at RPHL, Ernakulam showed presence of coliforms. Cleaning and chlorination of OHTs was done. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Mulavukad (CT), Sub-District Kanayannur, District Ernakulam. The cases presented with symptoms of loose stools and vomiting. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases were treated at CHC Kanayannur. Cases were in the age group 5 - 65 years. Cases had consumed food from a bakery. 2 water samples were collected from the tap of bakery and sent to Regional Public Health Laboratory, Ernakulam showed presence of coliforms. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water and food habits, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Kolari, Sub-district Iritty, District Kannur..Cases presented with symptoms of loss of appetite, abdominal pain and fever. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases were in the age group 6 - 38 years. All the cases were diagnosed based on symptoms and abnormal liver test results. Cases were treated at CHC Iritty. Out of 6 water samples collected and sent to RAL Lab Kuthuparamba, 3 samples were contaminated with Coliform and E. coli. Out of 2 blood samples collected and sent to Indira Gandhi Co-Operative Hospital Thalassery, 1 sample tested positive for Hepatitis A (IgM ELISA). ORS packets were given to cases. Super chlorination of wells was done. Community awareness and health education was given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Galaxy Inn Brilliant Girls Hostel, Village Mutholy (Ward No. 9), Sub-District Meenachil, District Kottayam. Cases presented with symptoms of fever, abdominal discomfort, nausea and vomiting. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The cases were in the age group 18 to 23 years. Cases were treated symptomatically. 2 water samples were collected from the hostel's well tank and filter unit and tested negative for E. coli and Coliforms at KWA Kottayam. Improper food storage, inadequate reheating, or cross contamination during food handling may have contributed to the outbreak. ORS packets were given to cases. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water and food habits, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of loose stool, abdominal pain, and vomiting were reported from Village Pudussery East, PHC Pudussery, Sub- District Palakkad, District Palakkad. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases were trainees in Forest Training Institute, Waalayar. Cases were in the age group 24-40 years. 2 stool samples collected were negative for salmonella, shigella and vibrio cholera. Cases treated symptomatically. Health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene maintenance and proper sanitation.

Cases of loose motion and vomiting were reported from Village Garra (CT), Sub- District Lalbarra, District Balaghat. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases treated symptomatically at a health camp organized in the locality. ORS packets and Zinc tablets distributed to cases by ASHA and ANM. 2 patients treated at a Private hospital. Cases were in the age group 2-77 years. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on use of boiled water for drinking purpose, hygiene maintenance and sanitation.

Cases of loose motion and vomiting were reported from Village Seridhana, PHC Hidli, Sub-District Athner, District Betul. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey done. Cases treated symptomatically. Cases were in the age group 5-65 years. 5 water samples collected and sent to DPHL Bhopal were non-potable. Chlorination of water sources was done in the village. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene maintenance and sanitation.

Cases of loose motion were reported from Village Chirmatekdi, PHC Bhaura, Sub- District Shahpur, District Betul. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey done Cases treated symptomatically by the peripheral team. 3 patients treated at CHC Shahpur. ORS packets and Zinc tablets given to cases. Cases were in the age group 9-55 years. 5 water samples collected and sent to DPHL Bhopal were non-potable. Chlorination of water sources was done in the village. Health education on hand hygiene and safe drinking water given to the community by peripheral team.

Cases of loose motion and vomiting were reported from Village Emlidhana, PHC Chirapatla, Sub-District Chicholi, District Betul. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was done. Cases treated symptomatically. Cases were in the age group 1-60 years. 1 stool sample collected and sent to DPHL Bhopal was invalid. Health education on hand hygiene and safe drinking water was given to the community by the peripheral team.

Cases were reported from Village Badgaon Mal, PHC Jawar, Sub-District Khandwa, District East Nimar. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases presented with fever and joint pain. The most affected age group was 15-44 years. Out of 12 serum samples collected and sent to District Hospital Khandwa, 11 samples tested positive for Chikungunya (IgM ELISA). Community awareness and health education were given by the peripheral team on vector control measures, hygiene, and sanitation. Sources identified included water collection on concrete surfaces and plastic waste

Cases were reported from Village Gidhauda, PHC Sarangpur, Sub-District Shahnagar, District Panna. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases presented with loose motion. People consumed water from a borewell in the affected area. Cases were treated at PHC Sarangpur. Cases were in the age group 1-77 years. 1 water sample collected by PHED was potable. Chlorination of water sources done by PHED. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene maintenance and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Devari Baghelan, CHC Naigarhi District Rewa. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases presented with loose watery stool, abdominal pain, vomiting after eating "kondo Rot" prasad at Matarani temple. Cases were treated at CHC Naigadhi. 1 patient was treated at Medical College Rewa. All cases recovered. 3 stool samples collected and sent to DPHL Rewa, tested negative for cholera by culture. Cases were in the age group 3-70 years. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe food habits.

Cases were reported from Village Ugna sehrana, CHC/Sub-District Karahal, District Sheopur. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Population of the affected area was 1034. House to house survey of 230 households was done. People consumed water from handpump and tubewell in the village. Cases were treated at a health camp organized in the locality and at CHC Karahal. Cases were in the age group 2 months - 65 years. 2 stool samples collected and sent to SRVS Medical College and Hospital Shivpuri tested negative for cholera (Hanging Drop preparation). 6 water samples collected by PHED were satisfactory for drinking purpose. 1 death occurred in a 2-month- old female on 16.07.2025 with symptoms of fever and breathlessness, 1 death in a 10-month- old male on 18-07-2025 with symptoms of loose motion, vomiting and fever, 1 death in a 28-year-old-male on 20- 07-2025 with severe dehydration and shock and a 17 months old male died on 24-07-2025. Chlorination of water sources was done by PHED. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene and sanitation

Cases of loose motion and vomiting were reported from Village Badkud, CHC/Sub- District Chitrangi, District Singrauli. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases treated symptomatically. Cases were in the age group 4-85 years. 1 water sample was collected and sent to DPHL Rewa showed growth of coliform bacteria by culture. Chlorine tablets distributed to households. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of loose motion and vomiting were reported from Village Katrihar, PHC Bagaia, Sub-District Chitrangi, District Singrauli.District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases treated symptomatically. Majority of the cases were in the age group 15-44 years. 1 stool sample collected and sent to DPHL Rewa tested negative for cholera by culture. 1 water sample was collected and sent to DPHL Rewa showed growth of coliform bacteria by culture. Chlorine tablets distributed to households. ORS packets and zinc tablets given to cases. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of fever with rash were reported from Village Mudiya, Para Khas & Para Ugad, CHC Badagaon, Sub-District Badgaon Dhasan, District Tikamgarh.District RRT investigated the outbreak. Active search for fever cases done in the locality. Cases treated symptomatically. Cases were in the age group 2-8 years. All 4 serum samples collected and sent to ICMR, Jabalpur tested positive for Measles (IgM ELISA). Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on isolation of cases, hygiene maintenance and proper nutrition.

Cases were reported from Village Asoda, and Patarkhede, Block Erandol, District Jalgaon. The cases presented with symptoms of fever with rash, cough, coryza and Conjunctivitis. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases were students of Ashramshala school. Cases were in age group 6 - 12 years. Cases were treated at GMC Jalgaon and RH Erandol. Out of 11 serum samples collected and sent to Kasturba Hospital Mumbai, 5 samples tested positive for Measles (IgM ELISA). Active search for left-out and drop-out vaccination cases was conducted, and special vaccination sessions were arranged for these beneficiaries. Vitamin A supplementation given to students of ashramshala school. Health education was given by the peripheral team on isolation of cases, hygiene maintenance and proper nutrition.

Cases were reported from Village Mawriangtynnai , PHC Kynrud, Block Mairang, District Eastern West Khasi Hills. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases presented with symptoms of vomiting, abdominal pain, headache, and loose stools. Cases had consumed leftover food. Cases were treated at PHC Kynrud and Nongum. The 15–19 years age group was identified as the most affected. 1 death occurred in a 15-year-old female on 14.07.2025 with symptoms of multiple episodes of vomiting and loose stools. Cause of death was AGE, Shock with Aspiration Pneumonia. Community awareness and health education on the importance of safe food and water handling practices was done by the peripheral team.

Cases were reported from Village Kuda (CT) & Dhansiri, UPHC Duncan, District Dimapur. Cases presented with fever, headache altered mental status, unconscious and neck rigidity. District RRT investigated the outbreak. 4 CSF samples of patients were confirmed for JE (IgM ELISA) on 11th July (1 case) and 16th July (3 cases) respectively at Sentinel surveillance site laboratory, District Hospital Dimapur. Cases had no travel history. A 48-year-old female died on 12- 07-2025 before the test result of confirmed JE was received. Second death occurred in a 80 -year -old male on 30-07-2025 with Bacterial Meningitis. Chronic Hepatitis B and Pulmonary TB were the other co- morbid conditions. Door -to -door fever surveillance was conducted, and fogging operations were carried out in the locality. Health education and community awareness were provided regarding JE symptoms, prevention, and vector control measures.

Cases of loose motion, vomiting and abdominal pain were reported from Village Remanda, PHC Remunda, Sub- District Bheden, District Bargarh. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases were students of Khiresara Meher High school. Cases were treated symptomatically. Cases were in the age group 11-15 years. ORS packets were distributed to the cases. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe food habits and drinking water, hygiene maintenance and proper sanitation.

Cases of loose watery stool were reported from Village Phasiguda, PHC BhismagirI, Sub-District Digapahandi, District Ganjam. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases treated symptomatically. Cases consumed stale food (kanji). Two cases treated at CHC Digapahandi & 4 cases treated at MKCG Medical College and Hospital, Berhampur Odisha. One stool sample collected tested negative for Cholera by culture. Cases were in the age group 5-71 years. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water and food habits, hygiene maintenance and proper sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Mohan Pada, PHC Mathalput, Sub-District Koraput, District Koraput. Cases are presented with fever, swelling and joint pain. Cases were in the age group 5 - 73 years. District RRT and VBD team investigated the outbreak. Aedes aegypti larvae were found in plastic drums and outdoor waste material in the community on investigation. All cases were treated at nearest health facilities. Out of 16 serum samples collected and sent to RMRC, Bhubaneswar, 10 samples tested positive for Chikungunya (IgM ELISA). The population of the affected area was 1066. Vector control measures undertaken in the community. IEC-BCC activities on anti- chikungunya measures with focus on source reduction done to create awareness and to minimize the formation of breeding source followed by personal protection and cleaning of peri-domestic areas (cutting of wild bushes-shrubs) by ASHA, ANM and Health Supervisor

Cases were reported from Village Patrapada, Sub-District Thakurmunda, District Mayurbhanj. Cases were students of Patrapada Ashram School who presented with loose motion, vomiting, nausea and abdominal pain after eating food prepared in the school kitchen. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases treated symptomatically. 4 cases treated at CHC Thakurmunda and 2 cases at SDH Anadapur. Cases were in the age group 7-19 years. Three rectal swabs and three water samples were collected. Water samples tested H₂S positive, with no residual chlorine detected on OT testing. Rectal swabs showed no enteropathogenic organisms. All samples were tested at DPHL, Mayurbhanj.1 stool and 2 rectal swab samples collected and sent to DPHL Mayurbhanj tested negative for cholera by culture. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe food habits and hygiene maintenance.

Cases of loose motion were reported from Village Nangalbod, Sub-District Sinapali, District Nuapada. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey done in the village. Symptomatic treatment given to cases. 3 cases treated at CHC Sinapali. Cases were in the age group 5-60 years. All 3 stool samples collected and sent to DPHL Balangir tested negative for cholera by culture. All 5 water samples collected tested positive for H S test. 2 Chlorine tablets were distributed to households. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene maintenance and proper sanitation.

Cases of loose motion were reported from Village Chelasi, Block Nawalgarh, Sub- District Nawalgarh, District Jhunjhunu. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected age group was 9-74 Years. The cases consumed food at an engagement ceremony. Cases treated symptomatically. Out of 10 stool samples collected and sent to DPHL Jhunjhunu, 8 samples showed growth of Staphylococcus aureus species. All 5 water samples collected were potable. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe food habits, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Mathiya, PHC Jiyanpura, Sub-District Sakaldiha, District Chandauli. The cases presented with symptoms of loose motion and vomiting. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The cases were of the age group of 1-55 years. Out of 4 water samples collected and sent to Regional Lab Swasthya Bhawan Lucknow, 1 sample was non-potable. People had consumed water from handpump in the affected area. Chlorine tablets distributed to households. ORS packets given to cases. Health education given regarding safe drinking water and hygiene maintenance.

Cases of loose motion and vomiting were reported from Village Durlavpur, Sub- District Saltora, District Bankura. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases were treated symptomatically. All 3 rectal swab samples collected and sent to BSMCH Bankura revealed common gut microbiota. All 5 drinking water samples collected from a well and tube well were contaminated with coliforms and E. coli. Chlorine tablets were distributed to households. ORS sachets and Zinc tablets were given to cases. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Peddakondayapalem, Sub-district lpur, District Palnadu. Cases presented with symptoms of stomachache, diarrhea and nausea. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases consumed food at a family function. Cases were treated symptomatically at a medical camp organized in the village. Cases were in the age group 38-70 years. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe food habits, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases reported from KGBV School, Village Papireddypalli, Sub-district Somandepalle, District Sri Sathya Sai. Cases presented with loose motion, vomiting and abdominal pain. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected age group was 14-70 years. Cases consumed food prepared in the hostel mess and were treated at PHC Somandepalli. Nine stool samples were collected and sent to DPHL, Hindupur. The results showed normal flora. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe food habits and clean drinking water, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Haresamudram, Sub-district Madakasira, District Sri Sathya Sai. Cases presented with the symptom of loose watery stools. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected age group was 5-60 years. House to house survey was done in the village and cases were treated symptomatically. Possible cause of the outbreak was water contamination. 3 water samples were collected and sent to RWS. One sample was non-potable. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene and sanitation.

Under Surveilla nce Cases reported from Village Gantakalla Golla Hatti, Sub-district Rolla, District Sri Sathya Sai. Cases presented with symptoms of loose motion and vomiting. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases were in age group 1 - 75 years. Cases were treated at a health camp organized in the village. Three stool samples were collected and sent to DPHL, Hindupur. The results showed presence of Aeromonas. Two deaths were reported: 10-year-old female (06.05.2025) and 21-year-old female (17.05.2025), both due to severe diarrhea and vomiting. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene and sanitation.

Under Surveilla nce Cases were reported from Villages Chichwahi and Gudaras, Sub-District Aundhi, District Mohla Manpur Ambagarh Chouki. Cases presented with symptoms of loose watery stools and vomiting. District RRT along with the Block RRT visited the affected villages to assess the situation and conducted a health camp to provide medical assistance. People consumed water from a common well. Cases were in the age group 15-65 years. It was observed that the well- used for drinking water was located adjacent to a septic tank, and there appeared to be seepage from the tank, possibly contaminating the well water. Water chlorination was done by the PHE department, Chlorine tablets were distributed to the households. Health education was given about safe drinking water, hygiene maintenance, proper sanitation and consumption of boiled water.

Under Surveilla nce Cases of fever less than 7 days, headache and myalgia were reported from Village Vadasserikkara, KAP-5 Police battalion ward 8, CHC Ranny Perunad, District Pathanamthitta. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases were treated at CHC Ranny Perunad and Ranni Taluk hospital. 2 throat swab samples collected and sent to NIV Alappuzha, tested positive for Influenza A (H3N2). Cases were in the age group 24-51 years. Health education given to the trainees in the camp by the District Surveillance Officer on spread of influenza and preventive measures, hygiene and sanitation.

Under Surveilla nce A case was reported from Engandiyur Panchayath, Sub-District Chavakkad, District Thrissur. District RRT investigated the outbreak. A 33 -year -old male presented with fever, sore throat, cough on 03/07/2025, followed by vesicles on hands and fingers the next day. The case had a history of travel from abroad on 14/07/2025. The patient was admitted to Aster Medicity, Kochi on 15-07-2025, with clinical symptoms provisionally diagnosed as Mpox. The case was diagnosed at Aster Medicity, Kochi, and the sample was tested at NIV Alappuzha on 16-07-2025 which was positive for Mpox by PCR. For confirmation, sample was further sent to NIV Pune on 18-07-2025, which was positive for Mpox (Clade I). The patient was cured and discharged from isolation at Government Medical College, Kalamassery, Ernakulam on 02.08.2025. Community awareness and health education on control, hygiene, and sanitation.

Cases of loose motion and vomiting were reported from Village Butwa, PHC Khatai, Sub-District Karahal, District Singrauli. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was done. Cases were treated symptomatically. Cases were in the age group 2-70 years.Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on hygiene and sanitation.

A case was reported from Village Chidimit Namesa, PHC Dagal, Sub-District Songsak, District East Garo Hills. A 31-year-old male presented with symptoms of fever, headache, muscle spasms, aerophobia, hyper salivation, insomnia, and hydrophobia. The case was clinically diagnosed as rabies. Based on history, the exposure occurred approximately five months prior, but the patient did not seek care or initiate treatment from any health facility. The patient was admitted to Williamnagar Civil Hospital on 7th July 2025 and succumbed to the illness on 10th July 2025. District RRT investigated the outbreak. As a precautionary measure, family members who were involved in patient care were advised to undergo post- exposure prophylaxis (PEP). Additionally, IEC activities were conducted, including a public health awareness campaign in the presence of the local headman, in collaboration with the District Veterinary Department, which organized a Mass Awareness Programme in Chidimit Namesa Village.

Cases of fever, body pain, and headache were reported from Village Koondankulam, PHC Navalady, Sub- District Radhapuram, District Tirunelveli. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Active search for fever cases done by the peripheral team. Cases treated at a health camp organized in the affected area. 3 cases were treated at KKMCH hospital. Cases were in the age group 18-51 years. Out of 35 blood samples collected and sent to KKMCH Tirunelveli, 15 samples tested positive for Dengue (IgM ELISA). A 35- year-old male died on 01.08.2025 with Sepsis, Shock with MODS, AKI, Respiratory Failure, Dengue+ve and Leptospirosis. Community awareness and health education were given by the peripheral team on vector control measures, hygiene, and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Villages Kuldoba and Baghakhuli, Sub-District Simlapal, District Bankura. Cases presented with loss of appetite, anorexia and abdominal pain. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases were treated at a medical camp organized in the affected area. Chlorination of water sources was done. Majority of the cases were below 20 years of age. All 10 serum samples collected and sent to STM, Kolkata tested positive for Hepatitis A (IgM ELISA). Pipeline leakages were repaired by PHED. Chlorination of water source was done. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases reported from VKV School, Tafragam, Lohit District with complaint of loose motion, abdominal pain and fever. After preliminary investigation by the RRT, five stool samples were collected for laboratory confirmation and sent to RMRC, ICMR Dibrugarh, Assam. All the samples were tested positive for E. Coli & Shigella Sonnei. Health camp was organized at VKV Tafragam on 25th & 26th Oct. 2022. All the infected patients after treatment fully recovered. Health education was given to all.

Case reported from PHC Rasikpur with symptoms of fever with headache. Eight blood sample sent to DPHL Lab Dumka for confirmation of IgM Dengue. Three blood samples found positive for dengue by IgM ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Health education was given.

Cases reported from Village Mudenur, PHC/CHC Batkurki, Taluk Ramdurag, District Belagavi with vomiting and loose stools. Three water and Eighteen stool, samples collected and send to BIMS Belagavi, where two water sapmles were found to be unsatisfactory and four stool samples culture showed growth of Vibrio cholera. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Health education was given.

Cases reported from Village Bandipalya, PHC/CHC Kadakola, Taluk Mysuru Rural, District Mysuru. Seven stool and six water samples collected and sent to DPHL Mysuru, No intestinal pathogen isolated in seven stool samples. Out of six water sample, one is Non potable, one is doubtful and rest four samples are potable. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Health education was given. RRT team visited village, house to house survey done, all cases are treated symptomatically on OPD basis at PHC , communication to panchayat regarding overhead tank clean and chlorination of water done

Cases reported from Village Hotpeth, PHC/CHC Shirwal, Taluk Shahapur, District Yadgiri. Two stool and four water samples collected and sent to DPHL Yadgiri where stool samples did not show any growth whereas water samples were found not suitable for potable purposes. The deceases was a 90 years Female. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Health education was given. House to house survey done. Water pipeline were repaired.

Cases reported from Palathara, Eravipuram, Kakkathoppu, Kollam Corporation. Nine samples sent to DPHL, KLM where five samples tested positive for Dengue by IgM ELISA. The deceased was a 35year old female. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Health education was given.

Cases reported from CHC Vilvattom, Thrissur Corporation, District Thrissur with loose stools and pain abdomen at a police academy. 15 Stool samples sent to Microbiology department at GMC Thrissur where they were found negative for Salmonella, Shigella and Vibrio. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Health education was given.

Cases reported from Village Lalapetai, HSC La Kudalur, PHC/Block Rishivandiyam, District Kallakurichi. Two Serum samples sent to King Institute, Guindy Chennai result awaited. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Health education was given. Vaccination of unvaccinated close contacts done. Infectious patients were isolated and treated.

Cases reported from Village Devaruppula KGBV, Mdl, Devaruppula, District Jangaon with loose stools and pain abdomen. Three water samples collected and sent to RWS, where one sample found not suitable for potable purposes. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Health education was given.

Cases reported from Village Pedda Shivanoor, SC Chetlat Himmaipaaly, HSC Chegunta, Toopran District Medak. Eleven water samples sent to RWS result awaited. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Health education was given.

Cases reported from Polakal Village, PHC Polakal, C Belagal Mandal, Kurnool District with symptoms of vomiting and loose stools. Water samples are sent for Regional Public Health Laboratory where out of four samples, two came positive for Klebsiella. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Safe drinking water from RWS was provided twice a day. House to house survey done by ANM and ASHA and given health education. Medical camp conducted 24/7 in the village.

Cases reported from village-Telicoat, PHC-Turekela, Block-Kharsia with loose motions and pain abdomen. Nine water samples were sent to PHE Raigarh, where coliform bacteria was found above permissible limit in all nine samples. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Door-to-door survey was done by health team. Chlorination of water was done. Health education was imparted regarding personal hygiene and environmental sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Araladinni, PHC/CHC Nidagundi, Taluk Bagewadi, District Vijayapura. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Ten Blood samples collected and sent to DPHL Vijaypura, where they all tested positive. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Health education was given.

Cases reported from Kalady, Thuravur, Kidangoor, District Ernakulam with symptoms of Mild fever, Myalgia, Maculopapular rash. No samples collected. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Health education was given. Vaccination of unvaccinated close contacts done. Infectious patients were isolated and treated.

Cases reported from Thrikkadavoor, Sakthikulangara, Ward 3 (St. Joseph Island, St. George Island, St Thomas Island, Fathima Island) Kollam Corporation. Twenty-Two samples sent to DPHL, KLM where14 samples sent to IAV Thonnakkal, TVM and all found positive for Dengue Type 2 serotype. The deceased was a 34 year female who died from dengue encephalitis. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Health education was given.

Cases reported from CHC Kanyakulangara, FHC Karakulam, (FWC Karakulam, FWC Earnikkara) District Thituvananthapuram with fever & Jaundice in a family. Three blood samples tested HAV Positive. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Health education was given.

Cases reported from Government Nurse Training Centre, Nagapattinam, Subcenter – Nagapattinam where 227 Nursing Students had taken Dosa for dinner. One of the students found one dead centipede in her dosa. One food and one water sample sent to DPHL Nagapattinam where food sample was found negative for salmonella, shigella, and vibrio cholera whereas water sample was found to be nonpotable. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Health education was given regarding Mess, Dining Hall And Cooking Place to be kept clean. Hand Washing facilities to be ensured. Symptomatic treatment given to affected.

Cases reported from Village Noonajore, SC Kaithia, PHC/Block Mahagama, District Godda. The cases presented with fever and maculopapular rash. Blood samples were sent to RIMS, Ranchi for further analysis, out of which four samples tested positive for Measles by IgM ELISA and two samples tested positive for Rubella by IgM ELISA. The most commonly affected age was 8 years. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Health education was given. Vitamin A was given to the affected cases.

Cases reported from Village Rhymbai PHC, District East Jaintia Hilla. Cases presented with diarrhea, vomiting, nausea and fever after consuming food at the community feast on the occasion of New Year celebration. The most commonly affected age was 20 years. The food that constituted of pork was likely the cause of the outbreak. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Health education was given regarding importance of properly cooked food and intake of safe drinking water.

Cases reported from Taluk Mangalore, District Dakshina Khannada. Cases presented with loose stools and nausea. Three water samples were collected and sent to DPHL Dakshin Kannada for bacteriological analysis. Out of all the samples, one water sample was found to be non-potable. District RRT investigated the outbreak and symptomatic treatment and ORS sachet were given to all cases. Health education was given on the importance of safe drinking water and hand hygiene.

Case reported from Poreyahat, Danre, Harijantola. District Godda. Cases reported with fever and vesicular rashes all over the body. Five blood samples were collected and sent to RIMS, Ranchi for IgM ELISA for Chicken Pox and it was found that four of these samples tested positive for chickenpox. District RRT investigated the outbreak, isolation of cases was done and symptomatic treatment was given to all the cases. Health education was imparted.

Cases reported from PHC Mellim, District South West Garo Hills Cases presented with fever and rash. District RRT investigated the outbreak and symptomatic treatment was given to all the cases. Health education was imparted.

Cases reported from village Patharkhumpa, SC Ambasaramunda, CHC Madhapur, Block Athamallik, and District Angul. Cases presented with symptoms of nausea and vomiting.
