Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on vaccination, hygiene and sanitation.

Case was reported from Sub-District Laskein, District West Jaintia Hills. A 6 year old female presented with complaints of fever, hydrophobia, and aerophobia. Cases were reported from Village Mailauna, Sub-District Gyanpur, District Bhadohi. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on vaccination, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases reported from Chandwa Block at Dhudhimati Village. Cases presented with fever and rashes. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases were isolated. Frequent changes of bedding and personal belongings, adequate diet and plenty of fluids were emphasized upon. Vitamin A Prophylaxis was given. Health education was given.

Case reported from Bhoovanahalli, Hasan District. Case presented with difficulty in swallowing, drooling, excessive salivation and headache. She had history of dog bite four months ago. The deceased case was a 50 years old female. Health education was given regarding the importance of post exposure prophylaxis.

Cases reported from Taluk Chincholi, District Kalaburagi. Cases presented with vomiting and loose stools. Five stool samples were sent for lab analysis. District RRT investigated the outbreak and house to house survey was conducted. All cases were given symptomatic treatment. Health education was given on the importance of safe drinking water and sanitation.

Case reported from Belekeri Village, Taluk Ankola, District Uttar Kannada. Case presented with fever, malaise and headache. One blood sample was sent to KMC Manipal and tested positive for Leptospirosis by IgM ELISA. The deceased case was a 35 years old female. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Active case search and mass fever survey was carried out. Health education was given regarding the importance of rodent control measures and proper disposal of wastes.

District RRT investigated the outbreak and house to house survey was conducted. All cases were given symptomatic treatment. Health education was given on the importance of safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases reported from Block Banda, District Sagar. Cases presented with loose stools. District RRT investigated the outbreak and house to house survey was conducted. All cases were given symptomatic treatment. ORS sachets were distributed. Health education was given on the importance of safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases reported from Pahami Village in Kolsa SC in Chichpalli PHC, Chandrapur. Cases presented with fever and bodyache. Four blood samples were sent to GMC Chandrapur. Three out of four samples tested positive for Plasmodium falciparum by Rapid Diagnostic Kit. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Fever survey and entomological surveillance in the area along with fogging was done. Breeding sources were eliminated. Health education was given regarding the importance of vector control measures.

Cases reported from Village Kendugudia, SC Sulsulia, CHC Bhatli, Block Bhatli, District Bargarh. Two rectal swabs and one water sample was sent for lab analysis. Health education was given on the importance of safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village – Sanarpatti, Subcenter – Sukkiravarpatti. Cases presented with fever and bodyache. Five blood samples were sent to DPHL, Virudhunagar. Anti-larval measures and source reduction was done. Indoor and outdoor fogging was done. Health education was given regarding the importance of vector control measures.

Cases reported from IIIT Basar, District Nirmal. Cases presented with loose stools, vomiting and abdominal pain. Water samples were sent to RIMS, Adilabad. Result awaited. District RRT investigated the outbreak and house to house survey was conducted. All cases were given symptomatic treatment. Health education was given on the importance of safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases of fever with parotid gland swelling were reported from GUPS School, Village Elavanchery, Sub- District Chittur, District Palakkad. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on isolation of cases, hygiene maintenance and proper nutrition.

Cases of loose watery stools, fever and vomiting were reported from Village Nigari, Block Bargi, Sub- District/District Jabalpur. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected age group was 6-65 years. 5 stool samples were tested at Microbiology Department, Medical College Jabalpur and no positive findings were reported. Chlorination of water sources was done. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of fever with joint pain were reported from Village Nimnagaon, Sub-District Nasrullaganj, District Sehore. Block RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house fever survey was done. Cases were treated at PHC Baibori. The affected age group was 20-80 years. 10 serum samples were tested at DH Sehore. 4 samples tested positive for Chikungunya (IgM ELISA). Anti-larval activities and fogging was done in the affected area. Community awareness and health

Cases of nausea, abdominal pain, fever and dark coloured urine were reported from Village Gadaheri, Sub-District Aheri, District Gadchiroli. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was done. Pipeline leakages were observed with mixing of sewage water and supply water. Cases were treated at a health camp established in the locality. Both children and adults were affected. Out of 7 blood samples collected and sent to DPHL Gadchiroli, 2 samples tested positive for Hepatitis A (IgM ELISA). All 8 water samples collected were potable. Chlorination of water sources was done. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of loose motion and vomiting were reported from Hyderbagh Ward, Millat Nagar, Galli No. 13, Sub- District/District Nanded. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Medicine and ORS packets were given to cases. The affected age group was 5-45 years. Out of 4 stool samples collected and sent to GMC Nanded, 2 samples tested positive for cholera by culture. Chlorination of water sources in nearby houses was done. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of fever with myalgia and fatigue were reported from Village Kalsuri, Sub-District Mhasla, District Raigad. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Active search for fever cases was done in the affected area. Cases were treated at PHC Mendadi. Cases of all age groups were affected. All 12 blood samples collected and sent to DH Alibag, tested negative for Dengue (NS1 ELISA). 1 death was reported of a 54 years-old-male on 17.11.2025 with symptoms of chest pain, weakness, fever and headache. Anti-larval activities and fogging was done. Community awareness and health education was given by the peripheral team on vector control measures, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of loose stools (>3 times a day) were reported from JNV School, Village Rymbai, Sub-District Khliehriat, District East Jaintia Hills. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Symptomatic treatment was given to cases. ORS packets were given to cases. Chlorine tablets were distributed to the households. Cases were mostly in the age group 5-14 years. 58 cases were screened, and blood samples were sent to the Pasteur Institute for testing, of which 28 tested positive for H. pylori. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene and sanitation.
Cases of fever with chills were reported from Village Netnyu, Sub-District Tamlu, District Longleng. District RRT

Cases of stomach ache, vomiting and loose motion were reported from Bapujinagar, Ward No-16, NAC, Boudh, Sub-District Baudh Sadar, District Boudh. Block and district RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected age group was 15-44 years. 2 water samples (from dug well and tube well) and 3 rectal swabs were tested at DPHL Boudh. The water samples tested positive for H S and OT<0.01 PPM. 2 Culture test for rectal swabs showed no enteropathogenic organisms. The patients were treated at VIMSAR Burla, Sambalpur District. A 34-year- old male died with the symptoms abdominal pain, vomiting, loose motion, weakness and discomfort on Date 26.11.2025. House to house survey was conducted and water disinfection was done. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water and food habits, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of fever were reported from Village Keelapalur, Sub-District Ariyalur, District Ariyalur. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Active search for fever cases was done in the affected area. Cases were treated at PHC Keelapalur. The affected age group was 1-63 years. 1 blood sample collected, tested positive for O. tsutsugamushi (IgM ELISA) in Ariyalur Medical College. Further, 4 blood samples and 3 water samples tested at DPHL, Vilangudi, Ariyalur showed no positive findings. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on vector control measures, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of fever with rash were reported from Village Kuttaimedu, Sub-District Bhavani, District Erode. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was done. Cases were students of primary school. All cases were treated symptomatically. The most affected age group was 6-10 years. 5 serum samples were tested at Kings Institute, Guindy, Chennai and all tested positive for V. zoster (IgM ELISA). The school administration was advised to isolate symptomatic cases for 7 days at home. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on proper hydration of cases, hygiene and sanitation.

A cluster of cases with fever and parotid gland swelling were reported from Shasthamkotta and Poruvazhy Panchayats, Blocks Sooranadu (137 cases) and Mynagapally (176 cases), Sub-District Kunnathur, District Kollam. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases gradually increased in October–November. The index case was a 6-year-old male from Poruvazhy Panchayat who self-isolated for 15 days. Children aged 5–6 years were most affected, and cases also occurred in adults. The outbreak spread rapidly through school buses, where children from different panchayats were in close, poorly ventilated contact, facilitating transmission. Inter-school attendance and household contacts further amplified spread, making containment challenging. Cases were treated symptomatically at health facilities and isolated at home. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on isolation of cases, hygiene maintenance and proper nutrition.

Cases of nausea, abdominal pain, loss of appetite and dark coloured urine were reported from Valanchery Municipality – Division 6, Sub-District Tirur, District Malappuram. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases were students of VHSS Valanchery and stayed at the school hostel. Cases frequently consumed food at nearby hotels. All cases were treated at PHC Valancheri. Cases were students of Higher Secondary and High School. 1 water sample collected from an open well (water source of the school) was potable. The affected age group was 13 to 17 years. 2 blood samples tested at RPHL Malapuram lab, were positive for Hepatitis A (IgM ELISA). Chlorination of water sources was done. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water and food habits, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of fever were reported from Village Uchale, Sub-District: Murbad, District Thane. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house fever survey was done. Cases were treated at PHC Narivali. Cases were in the age group 27-68 years. Out of 10 serum samples collected and sent to Civil Hospital Thane, 6 samples tested positive for Dengue (1 sample - NS1 ELISA and 5 samples - Rapid NS1). Fogging was done in the affected area. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on vector control measures, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of fever with myalgia and fatigue were reported from Village Changangei, Sub-District Patsoi, District Imphal West. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house fever survey was done. Cases were treated at PHC Khumbong. The affected age group was 12-63 years. Out of 16 blood samples collected from 03.11.2025 to 01.12.2025, 2 samples tested positive for Dengue (1 sample - IgM ELISA, 1 sample - NS1 ELISA). Anti- larval activities and fogging was done in the affected area. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on vector control measures, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of nausea, fatigue, loss of appetite, fever and dark coloured urine were reported from Dholabhata Area (Anandpuri, UIT Colony, Gahloto ki Dungari), Sub-District/District Ajmer. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was done. Cases were treated at a health camp established in the locality. Cases were in the age group 3-50 years. Out of 10 blood samples collected and sent to DPHL Ajmer, 9 samples tested positive for Hepatitis E (IgM ELISA). Out of 10 water samples collected, 3 samples were non-potable. Superchlorination of water sources was done by PHED. Chlorine tablets were distributed to the households. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene and sanitation.

Case reported from Village Atugaon, under PHC Panchapur, Block Bongaigaon, District Bongaigaon. Case presented with fever and headache followed by seizure and change in mental status. CSF sample was sent to FAAMCH, Barpeta and that came to JE IgM ELISA positive. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected case was 59 years old male. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on the importance of vector control measures.

Case reported as a part of ongoing AES outbreaks from various districts in Bihar in the year 2023. A total of 59 AES cases (19 from Muzaffarpur, 10 from Patna, 6 from Sitamarhi, 5 from East Champaran, 4 from Vaishali, 3 from West Champaran, 2 each from Bhojpur, Nawada and Saran, 1 each from Aurangabad, Jehanabad, Khagaria, Katihar, Samastipur and Sheohar districts) and 3 deaths (1 each from districts Nawada, Patna and Vaishali) have been reported. Case reported from Village Laxminiya, Block Dumri Katsari, District Sheohar. Case presented with difficulty in walking and urinary retention. Blood sample for JE IgM ELISA came negative. He was diagnosed with acute encephalitic syndrome by S.K.M.C.H, Muzaffarpur District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected case was 12-year-old male. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on the importance of vector control measures.

Cases reported from Village Mani, Taluka Kaprada, District Valsad. Cases presented with vomiting and diarrhea. Two water samples were sent to GMERS Medical College Valsad. Result showed recent fecal contamination in water sample. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected cases belonged to 7-16 years and 55-60 years age group. Cause of outbreak might be bovine colostrum from their pet cow. ORS sachets and zinc tablets were distributed. No deaths reported. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on the importance of food hygiene, safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Pallagatte, Taluk Jagaluru, District Davangere. Case presented with complaint of generalized weakness and B/L Lower limb weakness. District RRT investigated the outbreak. CSF and Saliva samples collected and sent to NIMHANS that came negative for Rabies viral RNA by real time PCR. Rabies virus neutralizing antibody titer by RFFIT in serum was 2048. Health education was given. Another victim of same dog bite event has been given PEP. 4 of his close contacts has been started with ARV. One death occurred of 49 years old male. Case had a history of dog bite on 30.03.2023. As PEP, wound toilet and ARV was given at Pallagatte PHC and was referred to GH Jagaluru for Immunoglobulins. But patient had ignored the concerned PHC MO advice. He had received 4 doses of ARV. On 28.04.2023, he has visited to PHC with complaint of generalized weakness and B/L Lower limb weakness later has been referred to DH, but was shifted to Yenepoya Medical Hospital, Mangalore on 28.04.2023. Case has succumbed to death on 03.05.2023.

Cases reported from Village/PHC Ucchangidurga, Taluk Harappanahalli, District Vijayanagar. Cases presented with Loose stools and vomiting with abdominal cramps. One water sample collected and sent to PHC Ucchangidurga, for bacteriological analysis. This was found suitable for potable purpose. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected cases belonged to 4-65 years age group. Cause of outbreak might be food poisoning (Sambar), as all 36 cases has history of having lunch from a private function at Renuka badavane, Ucchangi durga. ORS sachets and zinc tablets were distributed. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on the importance of food hygiene, safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases reported from Ward 15 (GMC Parippally Hostels, LH, MH, Inter’s Hostel) Kalakkode, Parippally, District Kollam. Cases presented with diarrhea, abdominal pain and nausea. Water samples from various sites were sent for lab analysis. These samples except from the kitchen site revealed fecal contamination and found to be unfit for drinking. While sample from kitchen site showed growth of E. Coli and Klebsiella. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected cases belonged to 20-26years age group. Cause of outbreak was found to be water. ORS sachets and zinc tablets were distributed. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on the importance of food hygiene, safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Chirakkal, SC Chirakkal, PHC Chirakkal, CHC Azhikode, District Kannur. Cases presented with fever, diarrhea, vomiting and abdominal pain. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cause of outbreak might be food consumed in the festival annadaanam (Feast) in Puzhathi Theru Shree Ganapathi temple. Cases reported from Village Morazha, under SC Main Centre Parassinikadavu, District Kannur. Cases presented with vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal discomfort and fever. ORS sachets and zinc tablets were distributed. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on the importance of food hygiene, safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases reported from Ward 24, 25 (Chalavara, Shornur, FWC Paruthipara, Mundaya), District Palakkad. Cases presented with loose stools, vomiting and stomachache. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on the importance of food hygiene, safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases reported from CHC Mattathur, CHC Kattoor, Karanchira, District Thrissur. Cases presented complaints of pain abdomen, loose motion and vomiting. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on the importance of food hygiene, safe drinking water and sanitation. One of the cases, a boy succumbed to death. His stool culture was positive for Shigella sonnie.

Cases reported from Urban Neemuch. Cases presented with fever with rash and Cough. District & block RRT investigated the outbreak. Out of this 3 came positive for IgM Measles Positive. Infected children were isolated and symptomatic treatment, Vitamin A given. Vaccination done for left out children. No deaths reported. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on the importance of sanitation.

Cases reported from villages Tentuliguda, Khajuriguda & Marichmal, Block Dasmantpur, District Koraput. Cases presented with painless skin sore, blister/bump in hand, neck forearms. Total 19 skin swabs specimen collected and tested at DPHL, Koraput which found positive for Bacillus Anthracis by Gram’s staining. Moreover, the RMRC, Bhubaneswar and NCDC team also visited to the affected villages for investigation. Etc. Animal vaccination and carcasses disposal are being done by district veterinary department. Total 6 Mini health cum surveillance camps conducted in the affected & nearby villages. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on the importance of hygiene and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Sanindipur, Block Koira, District Sundargarh. Cases presented with pain abdomen, vomiting and loose motion. District & block RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected cases were in the age group range of 2 to 62 years old. Water samples collected and tested through H2S which found negative. The possible source of infection was contamination of mixed curry in a death ritual community feast. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on the importance of food hygiene, safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Madkona, PHC Wagaon, Block Yavatmal, District Yavatmal. Cases presented with vomiting and headache. District & block RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected cases were in the age group range of 3 to 60 years old. Five water samples were collected and sent to DPHL Yavatmal for O.T test. The possible source of infection was food consumed at the private function held in a family. No food samples were available. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on the importance of food hygiene, safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Mangraul, Block Maheva, District Jalaun. Cases presented with fever with rash. 3 blood samples were sent to SGPGI Lucknow. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected cases belonged to 25-28 years age group. One sample came positive for IgM ELISA for the Chickenpox. Health Education was given on the importance of personal hygiene and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Padima Duan, Block Debra, District Paschim Medinipur. Cases presented with vomiting and loose motion. District & block RRT investigated the outbreak. Two rectal swabs collected and sent to MMCH, Medinapore. The possible source of infection was Prasad consumed on the occasion of Buddha Purnima Puja in a Grocery shop. No food samples were available. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on the importance of food hygiene, safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Borkatonee under PHC Sumonigaon, Block Charingia, District Golaghat. Cases presented with fever with blister. Samples could not be collected. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was done. Health Education was given on the importance of personal hygiene and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Adhalabheti under SHC Bhuegaon, Block Laharighat, District Marigaon. Case reported from Village Sarbaherua under SC Lailongpara, Block Orang, District Odalguri. Case presented with fever, headache and body pain. 1 serum sample was sent to DPHL Darrang and came positive for Dengue NS1 antigen. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected case 34 years old male. Fever survey was done Health Education was given on the importance of vector control measures.

Cases reported from Village Malahipur under CHC Chenari, District Rohtas. Cases presented with fever and rashes. Blood samples were sent for IgM ELISA Measles that came negative. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected case belonged to 5 years – 18 years age group. Health education was given on the importance of personal hygiene.

Cases reported from localities Nadiyal no Tekro, Kapodara, Sattadhar Soc., Ugam Nagar, Ranjit Ngar, Atalji Nagar, Of Fulpada UHC of East Zone – A of Surat Municipal Corporation. House to house survey was done and vitamin ‘A’ solution was administered to all cases. Extra Routine Immunization Sessions was conducted to cover due beneficiaries of MR1 & MR2 Vaccine and Extra MR dose up to 10 Years of Age. Health Education was given on the importance of immunization.

Cases reported from localities Ashapuri Soc-03, Akashdeep Soc., Laxmi Narayan Soc., Sai Baba Nagar of Pandesra UHC of South Zone – A of Surat Municipal Corporation. Cases presented with - Fever with Rash. 05 Serum Sample & 05 Throat Swab Sample collected and sent to, B.J Medical College, Ahmedabad. House to house survey was done and vitamin ‘A’ solution was administered to all cases. Extra Routine Immunization Sessions was conducted to cover due beneficiaries of MR1 & MR2 Vaccine and Extra MR dose up to 10 Years of Age. Health Education was given on the importance of immunization.

Cases reported from Village Chatro, Block Giridih, District Giridih. Cases presented with - Fever with Rash. 05 Serum Sample collected and sent to RIMS Ranchi. Of these 02 Samples were found positive for Measles by IgM ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected cases belonged to 04 months – 10 years age group. House to house survey was done and vitamin ‘A’ solution was administered to all cases. Extra Routine Immunization Sessions was conducted to cover due beneficiaries of MR1 & MR2 Vaccine and Extra MR dose up to 10 Years of Age. Health Education was given on the importance of immunization.

Cases reported from Village Sandosan, District Khunti. Cases presented with fever and rashes. 12 Blood samples were sent to RIMS Ranchi for IgM ELISA Measles that came negative. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected case belonged to 4 months to 36 years age group. Vitamin A given. Health education was given on the importance of personal hygiene.

Cases reported from Village Pervaje, PHC Bellare, Taluk Sullia, District Dakshina Kannada. Case presented with fever and pain in the abdomen. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected case was 59 years old male. One blood serum sent to DPHL Dakshin Kannada, result positive for Leptospirosis IgM ELISA. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team regarding the preventive measures. Case has succumbed to death on 30.04.2023.

Cases reported from Ward 10, Cheranellore, Thrikkakkara Municipality, District Ernakulam. Cases presented with fever with body ache. Three serum samples collected and sent to RPH Lab. All three samples came positive for Dengue ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Most affected age group was 30-45 years. Cause of outbreak is suspected to be water storing vessels and plastic containers. Vector indices found to be high. Health education was given.

Cases reported from Ward-9, SC Manneera, Block Panchayath Thannithodu, District Pathanamthitta. Cases presented with fever and generalized bodyache. Ten serum samples were sent for lab analysis. Of these, 8 samples were positive for Dengue NS1 and 2 Dengue IgM ELISA positive. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was done. The affected cases belonged to 4 to 74 years age group. Health education was given on the importance of vector control measures

Cases reported from Urban Neemuch. Cases presented with fever, vomiting and stomach pain. District & block RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected cases were in the age group range of 11-30 years. Cause of outbreak might be food poisoning as the affected students have eaten food in the hostel’s canteen and started having symptoms after 6 hours of taking meals. ORS sachets and zinc tablets were distributed. No deaths reported. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on the importance of food hygiene, safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Nongshluid under CHC Mawsynram, Block Mawsynram, District East Khasi Hills. Cases presented with fever and maculopapular rashes. Cases reported from Village Purbo Dayapur Block Udharbond, District Cachar. Case presented with dog bite history. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases reported from Village Patrabori and Torabori, Block Laharighat and Bhurbandha, District Marigaon. Cases presented with fever and jaundice. Serum sample were sent to GMCH. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on vector control measures and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Chhatapur, PHC Tuthi Panchayat, District Supaul. Cases presented with vomiting and loose stools. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases reported from Village Saloni, Block Gunderdehi, District Balod. Cases presented with vomiting and loose stools. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Door to door survey was done. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on food hygiene, safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases reported from CP tola Bagbeda District East Singhbhum. Cases presented with fever with rash. Three blood samples were sent to VRDL lab Jamshedpur in MGM Medical college. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, sanitation and importance of vaccination.

Cases reported from Village Kodadagudda, PHC Bilchodu, Taluk Jagaluru, District Davanagere. Cases presented with vomiting and loose stools after having food in a common event. Two water samples were sent to Bilchodu PHC Lab. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Water samples were negative in H2S media. Cause of outbreak might be food intake at an event, as symptoms appeared after having the food. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, sanitation.

Cases reported from ward 40, UPHC Bunder, Taluk Mangalore, District Dakshina Kannada. Cases presented with vomiting loose stools. Six water samples and one stool sample collected and sent to DPHL Dakshina Kannada. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Four water samples found unfit in MPN Method, stool sample did not show any enteropathogens. Age group of the cases were above 18 years. Cause of outbreak might be contaminated water. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Guladalli, PHC Kukanapalli, Taluk Koppal, Distirct Koppal. All cases had symptoms of vomiting & loose stools. Two stool and Seven water samples collected and sent to DPHL Koppal. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Out of 07 water samples, 03 were non-potable. 2 stool samples came positive for Vibrio Cholera by stool culture and sensitivity. Daily house to house survey was initiated along with ORS distribution. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Yaragunti, PHC Echanal, Taluk Lingasugur, Distirct Raichur. Cases presented with vomiting and loose stools. Eight stool samples and Forty-one water samples collected and sent to RIMS Lab. District RRT investigated the outbreak. One stool sample found positive for Vibrio cholerae by hanging drop method. Two water samples were found unfit for drinking in MPN method. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, sanitation.

Cases reported from ward- 16, Punnapra CHC Ambalapuzha, District Alappuzha. Cases presented with fever, headache. Twenty-Four samples collected and sent to PH Lab. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Twenty-two blood samples came positive for dengue (7 tested positive by IgM ELISA, 7 by NS1 ELISA, 1 by PCR and 7 by NS1 Card test). Source reduction and fever survey were done. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on vector control measures.

Cases reported from Panathady, PHC Konnakkad, District Kasaragod. Cases presented with nausea, vomiting, loose stools and pain abdomen. Two blood samples collected and sent to RPH Lab, Kannur. Affected age group is 15-17 years. One blood culture came positive for Spingomonas paucimobilis. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, sanitation.

Cases reported from Kalakkode, District Kollam. Cases presented with nausea, vomiting, pain abdomen and loose stools. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Case reported from Village Koppam, Irshadul Anam Sheriyath College, wards 3 District Palakkad. Cases presented with vomiting and loose stools. Result of water samples found unsatisfactory and presence of coliforms. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, sanitation.

Cases reported from Thrithala, Block Chalissey, District Palakkad. Cases presented with diarrhea, vomiting, fever and abdominal pain. Water samples collected and sent for testing. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cause of outbreak might be food intake at a marriage function at KMK Banquet hall Pattambi road, ward 3. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Panjal, SC Pynkulam, FHC Pazhayanur, District Thrissur. Cases presented with fever, loose stools and pain abdomen.
